result.title: Recovered or Memorized? Investigating Dynamical Consistency and Faithfulness in World Model Latents
result.comment: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Interpretability for Discovery (Interp4Discovery)
result.summary: World models develop internal simulators that can learn the structure and dynamics of an environment. It has been demonstrated that their internal representations are both meaningful and causal, but are these representations faithful to the governing dynamics of the environment they are learning? We introduce Anchored Recovery Certification (ARC), a procedure that utilizes a discrete Fréchet distance calculation with ground truth to evaluate dynamical consistency on candidate world models up to an affine gauge. We use the procedure on TD-MPC2 (decoder-free world model) that has learned the pendulum swing on an observation lift under varying hyperparameters at k = 5, 10, 25 steps. The model is then steered within a PCA-derived intervention subspace and compared against a ground-truth simulator using relative error to investigate dynamical faithfulness. ARC sufficiency held for TD-MPC2 most consistently at k = 10, with six of seven constraints statistically significant after Holm-Bonferroni correction, while the relative error between the simulator and the causal latent remained substantial. Further research could be conducted with decoder world models such as DreamerV3 (reconstruction loss) to investigate whether the results differ.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Anchored Recovery Certification（ARC），用离散 Fréchet 距离在仿射规范意义下衡量世界模型 latent 与真实动力系统的一致性，并在 TD-MPC2 单摆任务上通过 PCA 干预子空间检验其动态忠实性。
AI.relevance_reason: 「latent 是恢复动力学还是记住轨迹」的判据与干预式忠实性检验，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 是否真正承载任务动态而非记忆表面轨迹；但对象是 RL 世界模型，启发式迁移需自行判断。
